svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Transpiration: the loss of water vapour from the leaves, which pulls a stream of water up through the plant."], [1, "Root hairs absorb water from the soil by osmosis."], [3, "Water moves up the xylem as a continuous column, held together by cohesion and to the walls by adhesion."], [7, "In the leaf, water leaves the xylem and evaporates from the walls of spongy mesophyll cells into the air spaces."], [10, "Water vapour diffuses out through the open stomata into the drier air."], [13, "This loss creates tension that pulls more water up the xylem: the transpiration pull."]]
svg.title: Transpiration
svg.desc: Water absorbed by root hairs moves up the xylem to the leaves, evaporates from mesophyll cells into air spaces and diffuses out of the stomata; a magnified leaf section shows the tissues.
svg.text: Blue dots: liquid water. Pale dots: water vapour. Leaf section magnified.

g.data-info: Long thin extensions of root epidermis cells: a large surface area for absorbing water by osmosis (and mineral ions by active transport).
Most water is lost from leaves through stomata.
Dead, hollow, lignified tubes. Water moves up as a continuous column: water molecules stick together (cohesion, hydrogen bonds) and to the xylem walls (adhesion).
Waterproof layer that reduces water loss from the upper surface.
Tightly packed cells with many chloroplasts: the main site of photosynthesis.
Water evaporates from the moist walls of these cells into the air spaces, which become saturated with water vapour.
Xylem brings water into the leaf; phloem carries sugars away.
Guard cells open the stoma in light. Water vapour diffuses out, from high concentration inside to lower concentration in the air outside.

svg.text: air outside: lower water vapour concentration

g.data-info: Faster with more light (stomata open), higher temperature (faster evaporation and diffusion), wind (removes humid air), and lower humidity (steeper gradient).
g.text: The rate of transpiration increases with:
🌡 higher temperature: faster evaporation and diffusion
💨 wind: humid air blown away from the stomata
